THE FIRST LIST. GEM's Global Iron and Steel Tracker, June 2026 (V1), CC BY 4.0 by
the file's own About tab. 1293 plants worldwide; the census is of the 132 whose
`Country/area` is in the steel perimeter's named Europe — the EU, the United
Kingdom, Norway and Switzerland. THE SUBSET IS THE PUBLISHER'S OWN COLUMN, which
is the only reason a gap table over it may claim to sum to the list.
GEM'S FORWARD STATUS IS A CLAIM AND NEVER A CLASS. The unit tables say what GEM
knows, not what exists, and all 132 were searched against their owners' own
documents before any was classed — 823 fetches, gem.wiki used as a starting point
and never cited. Of the 95 plants GEM shows nothing forward at, ONE turned out to
carry an owner statement GEM has not recorded, and it is a question rather than
an admission.
THE 0.5 MTPA FLOOR IS GEM'S, NOT THIS REGISTER'S, and it bounds every coverage
figure below. GEM states it on its own About tab: "This database only includes
plants with crude iron/steelmaking capacity of five hundred thousand tonnes per
annum (0.5 mtpa) and greater." The steel perimeter has NO tonnage threshold,
deliberately. So a works under half a million tonnes cannot appear in this table
at all, and no figure here may be read as coverage of European steel. LeadIT sets
no capacity floor and is the second list for exactly that reason; until it is in,
every number below carries the floor.

P100000120453.clause: fuel switch, no primary route change
P100000120453.ruling: RULED 16 September 2026, on question S1. A HYDROGEN-READY FURNACE MEANS THE UNIT THAT MAKES IRON OR STEEL — a DRI shaft, an EAF, or a furnace the owner states replaces blast-furnace capacity. Hydrogen fed to reheat or burner equipment is a fuel switch and is outside the perimeter.
P100000120453.note: THE WORKS' STEELMAKING FURNACE IS AN EXISTING SCRAP EAF AND NOTHING REPLACES IT. What the investment changes is the fuel in the burners and the iron that arrives from somewhere else. THE IRON IS THE POINT AND IT IS MADE AT GIJÓN: Sestao's own zero-carbon claim rests on a DRI plant at another works, which this census admits as its own entry. Recorded there as a location statement rather than here as a project, so the tonne is counted once and at the place it is made.
P100000120453.question: Is hydrogen fired in a works' BURNERS a 'hydrogen-ready furnace' for the steel perimeter, at a works whose steelmaking furnace is an existing scrap EAF?
P100000120453.speaker: ArcelorMittal, own announcement with the Government of Spain
P100000120453.verbatim: In addition to the investments in the DRI and EAF installations in Gijón, ArcelorMittal will invest €50 million in Sestao. This, together with the green DRI and hydrogen feeding the burners, will result in the Sestao plant achieving zero carbon-emissions.
P100000120453.why_the_rules_did_not_settle_it: The perimeter's four legs are an announced DRI plant, an EAF replacing blast-furnace capacity, greenfield DRI/EAF primary steelmaking, and a hydrogen-ready furnace. Sestao has no blast furnace, is not greenfield, and its DRI is at GIJÓN — a different works, already admitted. What is at Sestao is €50 million and hydrogen fed to burners. Whether that is 'a hydrogen-ready furnace' turns on whether the leg means the steelmaking furnace or any furnace at the works, and the rule does not say.
P100000120453.rule_would_need_to_say: Whether 'hydrogen-ready furnace' names the vessel that makes the steel, or any fired equipment at the works. If the former, Sestao is refused and its zero-carbon claim rests on iron made elsewhere; if the latter, reheat and annealing furnaces across the sector come into scope.
